capabilities: Browse the vault one folder at a time with breadcrumb navigation
Toggle between the drill-down list and the native file tree
Color-code folders with a tint that carries to subfolders
Reveal the active note in the folder list
Create, rename, move and delete files from the context menu
extras: The README warns that a major Obsidian update may break the takeover since it replaces a core view through the public API, with a safe fallback to the native file list. Mobile is supported but mainly exercised on desktop. It works around Obsidian core context-menu items not firing on the file-menu event by rebuilding them itself.
intentEvidence: replaces the sidebar file tree with drill-down navigation — the sidebar shows one folder at a time
motivation: The author wanted constant-depth sidebar navigation, like double-clicking into folders in Windows Explorer or macOS Finder, because indentation eats the width of a narrow sidebar.
problem: Obsidian's indented file tree squeezes file names into a sliver at deep folder levels and keeps the whole tree on screen competing for attention.
summary: Replaces the sidebar file explorer with drill-down navigation that shows one folder at a time and a breadcrumb to climb back up.
